statuses.lawful-with-conditions: lawful, with conditions named in the row
statuses.residents-only: lawful, but not for a non-resident
statuses.no-data: nobody here has read the law

note: A row is a reading of one named instrument on one date. Law moves; a row older than its country's last reform is wrong, and the date is printed beside every cell so a reader can see how old it is. Nothing here is legal advice.

rows.subject: cyprus
rows.conditions: Medically assisted reproduction is regulated by statute and practised through units working under the framework the Council of Medically Assisted Reproduction publishes; the terms have been amended four times since 2015.
rows.instrument: Medically Assisted Reproduction Law 69(I)/2015, as amended by 194(I)/2015, 92(I)/2016, 113(I)/2018 and 166(I)/2023
rows.note: the Council's own legal-framework page names the law and its amendments. This row records that the statute governs and is current; the detailed conditions inside it are for the donor-anonymity and surrogacy rule records, each with its own reading and date.

rows.subject: north-cyprus
rows.conditions: Assisted reproduction centres operate under the Turkish Cypriot Ministry of Health, which publishes a regulation numbered 381/2016 made under Article 32 of the law on those centres. The regulation's terms were not read for this record: the ministry's copy is a scan.
rows.instrument: Üremeye Yardımcı Tedavi Merkezleri regulation 381/2016, made under Article 32 of the assisted reproduction centres law, Ministry of Health, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus
rows.note: the row records that a licensing regime exists and who runs it. It does not state what is permitted under it, and it should not be read as saying any particular treatment is lawful here.

rows.subject: portugal
rows.conditions: Medically assisted procreation is governed by Law 32/2006 as amended; in Ruling 225/2018 the Constitutional Court considered the surrogacy and donor-anonymity provisions of that law against the constitutional right to know one's origins.
rows.instrument: Law 32/2006 on medically assisted procreation, as amended by Laws 17/2016 and 25/2016; Constitutional Court Ruling 225/2018
rows.note: read from the court's own English summary page. The row is dated 2018 and later amendments to the law are not read here; a stale row is a wrong row, and the donor-anonymity rule record carries its own reading.

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.instrument: Wet afbreking zwangerschap (Wet van 1 mei 1981), articles 3 and 6, as amended in 2022
rows.note: No week limit in the Act itself and no residence or nationality bar; the word woonplaats appears only in the article 11 statistical reporting. The fixed five-day waiting period was removed by the Act of 22 August 2022 and the doctor and the woman now set the term together.

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Grounds-based: two registered medical practitioners must be of the opinion, formed in good faith, that a ground is met, and the treatment must be at an approved place. Ground (a) runs to 24 weeks. There is no residence or nationality requirement anywhere in section 1.
rows.instrument: Abortion Act 1967, section 1
rows.note: Section 7(3): the Act does not extend to Northern Ireland, which has its own arrangements.

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Twelve weeks on written request for a resident — but § 10 bars the procedure for foreign women who are in the country only temporarily. A second termination within six months is also barred.
rows.instrument: Zákon č. 66/1986 Sb., o umělém přerušení těhotenství, §§ 4 and 10
rows.note: The text is unamended and in force. The WHO Global Abortion Policies Database's additional-restrictions note for Czechia records the six-month rule and physician refusal but not § 10; the statute was read directly for this row.

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Twenty-four weeks, but section 3 confines treatment to citizens, wives of citizens, work-pass holders and their wives, or a person resident in Singapore for at least four months immediately preceding — the only exception being where the procedure is necessary to save the woman's life. A two-day waiting period follows counselling.
rows.instrument: Termination of Pregnancy Act 1974, section 3, with the Termination of Pregnancy Regulations 1987

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Twelve weeks, with a waiting period of not less than three days. There is no residence bar on lawfulness — section 20 expressly contemplates a woman who resides outside the State — but free care is confined to the ordinarily resident, which is a funding rule and not a legal one.
rows.instrument: Health (Regulation of Termination of Pregnancy) Act 2018, section 12

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Twelve weeks, after mandatory counselling and a wait of at least three days before the procedure. No residence condition.
rows.instrument: Strafgesetzbuch § 218a, with § 219

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Fourteen weeks at the woman's request. Article 3.2 extends the rights it sets out to all persons present in Spain.
rows.instrument: Ley Orgánica 2/2010, artículos 3, 13 bis y 14

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: To the end of the fourteenth week on request; the article carries no residence condition.
rows.instrument: Code de la santé publique, article L2212-1, as amended by loi n° 2022-295

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Twelve weeks from conception, and not until six days after the first consultation.
rows.instrument: Loi du 15 octobre 2018 relative à l'interruption volontaire de grossesse, article 2

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Ten weeks by the woman's choice, after a reflection period of not less than three days.
rows.instrument: Código Penal, artigo 142.º, as amended by Lei n.º 16/2007

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Grounds only: danger to life or health, and pregnancy resulting from a criminal act. The fetal-defect ground was struck down by the Constitutional Tribunal in 2020.
rows.instrument: Ustawa z dnia 7 stycznia 1993 r. o planowaniu rodziny, ochronie płodu ludzkiego i warunkach dopuszczalności przerywania ciąży (Dz.U. 1993 nr 17 poz. 78)

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Ten weeks on request, and the consent of the husband is required for a married woman.
rows.instrument: Nüfus Planlaması Hakkında Kanun (Kanun No. 2827), Madde 5 ve Madde 6

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Twelve weeks from the last menstrual period, on the written request of a woman invoking distress, after an in-depth consultation.
rows.instrument: Code pénal suisse, articles 118, 119 et 120

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.instrument: Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, 597 U.S. 215 (2022)
rows.note: Federal position only. There is no federal right and no federal prohibition; state law governs, and the WHO database codes every field for the United States as varying by jurisdiction. This project has read no state statute for this row.

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Twelve weeks at the woman's request. No spousal consent, no parental consent, no counselling requirement, and no citizenship or residence bar recorded.
rows.instrument: Choice on Termination of Pregnancy Act 92 of 1996, as amended in 2008, with Regulation 168 of 1997

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: The first three months on request; no spousal or parental consent recorded.
rows.instrument: Code pénal, article 214

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Grounds-based rather than on request. Only the consent of the woman is required; a guardian consents under 18.
rows.instrument: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act 1971, with the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act 2021

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: On request to 12 weeks. Between 12 and 20 weeks an examination and counselling on alternatives are required under a 2022 decree.
rows.instrument: Criminal Code sections 301 and 305, as amended by the Criminal Code Amendment Act (No. 28) B.E. 2564 (2021)

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Grounds-based, including economic grounds, and the consent of the spouse is required — waived only where the spouse is unknown, cannot express an intention, or is dead.
rows.instrument: 母体保護法 (Maternal Health Act, Act No. 156 of 1948), article 14

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Rape or sexual violence, or a medical emergency. The husband's permission is required except for victims of rape, and counselling is mandatory.
rows.instrument: Undang-Undang No. 17 Tahun 2023 tentang Kesehatan, with PP 28/2024 and the 2023 Criminal Code

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.instrument: Revised Penal Code (1930), articles 256 to 259
rows.note: Criminalised in all circumstances; the database records no legal ground.

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: No criminal abortion law and no gestational limit in federal law. Provincial insurance coverage varies, which is a funding question rather than a legal bar.
rows.instrument: R. v. Morgentaler, [1988] 1 S.C.R. 30, with the Canada Health Act

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.conditions: Federal criminalisation has been struck down, and the position is governed mainly at state level rather than nationally. This project has read no state code.
rows.instrument: Federal Penal Code as amended, with Supreme Court decisions 2017/148 (2021) and 267/2023

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.note: The WHO database codes Romania as grounds-based with termination on request recorded as unavailable, which conflicts with the usual reading of article 201 of the Criminal Code. The Romanian statute database refused the connection on this pass, so the conflict is left open rather than resolved.

rows.subject: abortion-travel-law
rows.note: State and territory law, not federal. The WHO database codes every field as varying by jurisdiction and lists no state act; no state act was read on this pass.

rows.subject: assisted-dying-law
rows.subject_name: Assisted dying, and who may cross a border for it
rows.conditions: The article punishes inciting or assisting suicide only where the person acts from a selfish motive. It sets no nationality condition and no residence condition, which is why Switzerland admits people who live elsewhere.
rows.instrument: Swiss Criminal Code, Article 115
rows.note: Read on this pass at a private reproduction of the statute because the federal portal renders by script; the SR number is therefore not printed from that reading.

rows.subject: assisted-dying-law
rows.subject_name: Assisted dying, and who may cross a border for it
rows.conditions: Six due-care criteria, among them that the physician be satisfied the request is voluntary and well-considered and the suffering unbearable with no prospect of improvement, and that a second independent physician has seen the patient. The Act carries no nationality or residence clause; the gate is the treating relationship those criteria presuppose.
rows.instrument: Wet toetsing levensbeëindiging op verzoek en hulp bij zelfdoding, artikel 2

rows.subject: assisted-dying-law
rows.subject_name: Assisted dying, and who may cross a border for it
rows.conditions: Adult or emancipated minor, capable and conscious, a voluntary, considered and repeated request, a hopeless medical situation and constant unbearable suffering. No nationality or residence condition appears in the article.
rows.instrument: Loi du 28 mai 2002 relative à l'euthanasie, article 3

rows.subject: assisted-dying-law
rows.subject_name: Assisted dying, and who may cross a border for it
rows.conditions: Spanish nationality, or lawful residence in Spain, or a municipal register certificate showing more than twelve months in Spanish territory.
rows.instrument: Ley Orgánica 3/2021 de regulación de la eutanasia, artículo 5.1.a)

rows.subject: assisted-dying-law
rows.subject_name: Assisted dying, and who may cross a border for it
rows.conditions: French nationality or stable and regular residence in France, as one of five cumulative conditions.
rows.instrument: LOI n° 2026-794 du 18 août 2026 relative à l'aide à mourir, article 4, inserting Code de la santé publique article L. 1111-12-2
rows.note: A statute a month old at the date of this reading. Read on this pass by a research agent rather than by the author of this record; treat the article reference as unconfirmed by a second reader.

rows.subject: assisted-dying-law
rows.subject_name: Assisted dying, and who may cross a border for it
rows.conditions: Eligibility is keyed to entitlement to health services funded by a government in Canada, forgiving only any applicable minimum period of residence or waiting period. A visitor with no provincial entitlement is not reached by that saving clause.
rows.instrument: Criminal Code (R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46), section 241.2(1)(a)

rows.subject: assisted-dying-law
rows.subject_name: Assisted dying, and who may cross a border for it
rows.conditions: The two states read here run opposite rules. Oregon's current text carries no residency clause: the requirement was removed in 2023 after a federal suit settled. California requires the applicant to be a resident of California, proved by a driver's licence or state identification, voter registration, property ownership or lease, or a recent state tax return.
rows.instrument: No federal statute read for this row; state law governs. Oregon Death with Dignity Act, ORS 127.805, as amended by Or. Laws 2023 ch. 241 § 2, and California End of Life Option Act, Health and Safety Code § 443.2(a)(3), are the two read here.
rows.note: The federal position and the other states with such statutes were not read on this pass.

rows.instrument: Suicide Act 1961, section 2, as substituted by the Coroners and Justice Act 2009
rows.note: An act capable of encouraging or assisting suicide, done with intent, is an offence whether or not a suicide follows. Maximum 14 years.

rows.subject: donor-anonymity-law
rows.conditions: Anonymity is compulsory, not optional: the donation is anonymous and the confidentiality of identity data must be guaranteed. Disclosure is possible only exceptionally, in extraordinary circumstances carrying a definite danger to the life or health of the child.
rows.instrument: Ley 14/2006 sobre técnicas de reproducción humana asistida, artículo 5.5
rows.note: Spain is the largest egg-donation destination in Europe, and this article is one reason. Its national registry recorded 27,564 cycles in 2022 for patients resident in other countries, 52.3% of them using donated eggs.

rows.subject: donor-anonymity-law
rows.conditions: Anonymity ended for donations made from 1 April 2005. A person conceived from such a donation may obtain non-identifying details at 16 — physical description, year and country of birth — and identifying details at 18, including the donor's full name now and at birth. Donations between 1 August 1991 and 31 March 2005 release non-identifying information only, and nothing is held from before August 1991.
rows.instrument: The Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority (Disclosure of Donor Information) Regulations 2004 (SI 2004/1511)
rows.note: The Authority's own page is the practical statement of what is released and when.

rows.subject: donor-anonymity-law
rows.conditions: A national sperm-donor register holds the donor's identity and a person conceived may apply for disclosure from the register.
rows.instrument: Samenspenderregistergesetz (SaRegG) § 10

rows.subject: donor-anonymity-law
rows.conditions: Donor data are held by a statutory foundation and released to the person conceived on request at the age the Act sets.
rows.instrument: Wet donorgegevens kunstmatige bevruchting

rows.subject: donor-anonymity-law
rows.conditions: A person conceived by donation who is sufficiently mature has the right to information about the donor.
rows.instrument: Lag (2006:351) om genetisk integritet m.m., 6 kap. 5 §

rows.subject: donor-anonymity-law
rows.conditions: The provider must preserve mutual anonymity between the anonymous donor and the infertile couple, and between the donor and the child born. Section 6(1) confines treatment to a woman and a man who undergo it together.
rows.instrument: Zákon č. 373/2011 Sb., o specifických zdravotních službách, § 10(1)

rows.subject: donor-anonymity-law
rows.note: Two readings conflict and this project has resolved neither. The Constitutional Court's ruling 225/2018 heard a challenge to donor anonymity under article 15 of Lei 32/2006, argued against the child's right to know its origins under article 26 of the Constitution; the ESHRE survey's position at 31 December 2022 groups Portugal with the strict-anonymity states. The Portuguese instrument in its current form was not read.

rows.subject: gender-affirming-care-access
rows.conditions: A court's permission is a precondition of the surgery itself, not only of the later change to the civil register: the applicant must be over 18, unmarried, and hold an official health-council report from a training and research hospital. A second court step follows the surgery for the registry change.
rows.instrument: Turkish Civil Code, Article 40
rows.note: The requirement of permanent incapacity to procreate was struck by Constitutional Court decision 2017/165, which this project has not read. Whether Article 40 binds a foreign patient treated in Türkiye is not answered by anything read on this pass, and Türkiye is a destination for this surgery — so this is the gap in the table that matters most.

rows.subject: gender-affirming-care-access
rows.conditions: Adults are not restricted: article 6 permits private supply of these medicines to people aged 18 and over. Article 4 is the general prohibition the exemptions run from.
rows.instrument: The Medicines (Gonadotrophin-Releasing Hormone Analogues) (Restrictions on Private Sales and Supplies) Order 2024 (SI 2024/1319)
rows.note: Article 8 bars new private prescriptions of gonadotrophin-releasing hormone analogues for puberty suppression in under-18s, except for patients who had started before 3 June 2024 in England, Wales and Scotland or 27 August 2024 in Northern Ireland. Article 5 leaves NHS supply unaffected. The Order carries no expiry; article 9 requires a first review before 1 October 2027 and then at intervals of no more than four years.

rows.subject: gender-affirming-care-access
rows.conditions: The Supreme Court held that Tennessee's statute is not subject to heightened scrutiny and satisfies rational-basis review. The Court expressly did not decide the position for adults.
rows.instrument: No federal instrument governs adult access; state law governs. United States v. Skrmetti, No. 23-477, decided 18 June 2025.
rows.note: For minors, a named tracker with its own date: the Movement Advancement Project records 26 states and one territory banning this care for minors as of 16 September 2026, six of them making it a felony, with enforcement blocked by court rulings in Montana and Kansas at that date.

rows.subject: gender-affirming-care-access
rows.conditions: For adults, informed consent alone: no judicial or administrative authorisation, and the care sits within the compulsory medical programme.
rows.instrument: Ley 26.743 de Identidad de Género, artículo 11, as amended by Decreto 62/2025
rows.note: Decreto 62/2025, published 6 February 2025, bars hormonal and surgical intervention for under-18s. A federal appeal court in Paraná is reported to have held the decree unconstitutional; this project has not read that judgment.

rows.subject: gender-affirming-care-access
rows.conditions: Surgical sex change at 18 or over, on written application and the unanimous positive opinion of an expert commission established by the Ministry of Health, made up of health professionals and a lawyer with knowledge of medical law; the commission must act within three months. Where the patient's legal capacity is restricted a court must also consent. The provisions contemplate an extract from medical records kept in another state, with a certified translation.
rows.note: The reference to foreign medical records is the only thing read on this pass in any of these statutes that speaks to a patient who comes from elsewhere.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.conditions: Altruistic only; the intended mother must be medically unable to carry, must reside in Greece, and a family court approves the agreement before embryo transfer. Maximum intended-parent age 50, extendable to 54. The surrogate must be 25 to 50 and may act at most twice. Expenses are capped: EUR 10,000 for physical strain in a single pregnancy, EUR 15,000 for a multiple, and lost income capped at EUR 10,000.
rows.instrument: Law 3089/2002 amending the Civil Code, with Law 3305/2005 on medically assisted reproduction
rows.note: 81 children were born from surrogacy arrangements in 2022 and 51 in 2023, on the figures the briefing carries.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.conditions: Altruistic only; a special body consents and a family court approves before transfer. The surrogate must normally reside in Cyprus, with one exception: if no surrogate can be found, one residing abroad may be used provided she is in Cyprus from the 28th week.
rows.instrument: Medically Assisted Reproduction Law 2015 (69(I)/2015), Articles 22 to 27
rows.note: 21 applications in 2022 and 10 in 2023, all approved except one each year. More detailed decrees are envisaged.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.conditions: Altruistic only, and the implementing regulation is still missing: the law entered into force on 1 January 2022, and on 13 January 2024 the President referred a draft regulation back to the government. Without it the route does not run.
rows.instrument: Lei 90/2021, amending Lei 32/2006 on medically assisted procreation
rows.note: Two earlier attempts, Lei 25/2016 and its amended successor, were held unconstitutional in rulings 225/2018 and 465/2019, chiefly over the surrogate's inability to withdraw consent.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.conditions: Altruistic only; the relevant sections were not yet in force at the briefing's date. At least one intended parent and the surrogate must have resided in Ireland for two years; intended parents must be 21 or over; at least one must be genetically related to the child; a parental order is made by a court between 28 days and six months after birth.
rows.instrument: Health (Assisted Human Reproduction) Act 2024

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.instrument: Ley 14/2006 sobre técnicas de reproducción humana asistida, artículo 10
rows.note: The contract is null of full right, with or without payment, and parentage follows the birth. The same prohibition stood in article 10 of the predecessor Ley 35/1988.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.instrument: Embryonenschutzgesetz § 1(1)(7), with Adoptionsvermittlungsgesetz Article 13c
rows.note: The Embryo Protection Act penalises the medical professional with up to three years; the adoption placement act prohibits the arrangement itself.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.instrument: Article 31 of Law NN 86/12 on medically assisted reproduction

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.instrument: Article 11 of Law XII-2608 on Assisted Reproduction

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.instrument: Article 12(6) of Legge 40/2004
rows.note: Three months to two years' imprisonment. Amended in November 2024 to reach Italian nationals who conclude a surrogacy agreement abroad — the only extraterritorial clause among the Member States the briefing surveys.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.instrument: Code civil, article 16-7
rows.note: Any surrogacy agreement has been null and void since 1994.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.instrument: Implicit prohibition under the assisted reproduction rules, which confine treatment to a marriage or registered partnership
rows.note: The briefing groups Hungary with Austria, Estonia, Finland and Sweden as implicit bans and names no article; this project has not read the Hungarian instrument.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.note: Recorded as unregulated, which means arrangements happen but parentage and enforcement are unsettled. No Czech instrument was read for this row.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.conditions: Closed to foreign intended parents by definition: section 2(h) defines a couple as "the legally married Indian man and woman", and section 2(s) defines an intending woman as an Indian widow or divorcee aged 35 to 45. Altruistic only. A medical indication is required, certified by a District Medical Board; the couple must be married and aged 23 to 50 (female) and 26 to 55 (male); they must have no surviving child; and a magistrate's order on parentage and custody must precede the procedure.
rows.instrument: The Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021 (Act No. 47 of 2021), sections 2(h), 2(r), 2(s) and 4
rows.note: A couple of Indian origin must obtain a certificate of recommendation from the Board.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.conditions: The intending parents must be adult Thai citizens, or where only one is Thai must have been married at least three years, and must be a legally married couple whose wife cannot conceive. Commercial surrogacy, trade in gametes and embryos, brokering and promotion are prohibited.
rows.instrument: Protection for Children Born through Assisted Reproductive Technologies Act, B.E. 2558 (2015), section 21(1)
rows.note: Enacted 19 February 2015 after a scandal over a surrogate child abandoned by foreign intended parents; in effect 30 July 2015. Surrogacy for profit carries 10 years and up to 200,000 baht; acting as an agent, 5 years and up to 100,000 baht.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.conditions: The agreement must be confirmed by the High Court before artificial fertilisation, and the chapter ties the arrangement to domicile in the Republic.
rows.instrument: Children's Act 38 of 2005, Chapter 19 (surrogate motherhood agreements)
rows.note: This project read the Act's chapter heading and structure; the domicile subsection was not quoted on this pass.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.conditions: Altruistic only: negotiating a surrogacy arrangement on a commercial basis and advertising are offences under the 1985 Act. The agreement is unenforceable, and parenthood transfers only by a parental order under section 54, which requires at least one applicant to be domiciled in the United Kingdom.
rows.instrument: Surrogacy Arrangements Act 1985, sections 2 and 3, with the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Act 2008, section 54

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.conditions: Paying a surrogate, offering to pay, or advertising such payment is an offence; reimbursement of receipted expenditure is permitted under the regulations. Parentage is provincial law.
rows.instrument: Assisted Human Reproduction Act (S.C. 2004, c. 2), section 6

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.conditions: California's section requires separate independent counsel for the surrogate and the intended parents, notarised signatures, and disclosure of how the intended parents will cover medical expenses. It carries no residency requirement and no cap on compensation. Other states prohibit or restrict the arrangement; this project has read no other state's code.
rows.instrument: No federal statute; state law governs. California Family Code § 7962 is the example read for this row.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.note: Georgia is widely described as permitting commercial surrogacy for foreign intended parents, and a restriction has been announced repeatedly since 2023. The consolidated Law of Georgia on Health Care could not be read to its Article 143 on this pass, and this project will not print an article it has not read.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.note: Ukraine is one of the largest destinations for commissioned surrogacy. No Ukrainian instrument was read on this pass.

rows.subject: surrogacy-law
rows.note: Surrogacy in Australia is state and territory law, and some states reach arrangements made abroad. No state act was read on this pass.

rows.subject: transplant-prohibition
rows.subject_name: Buying an organ, and being transplanted abroad
rows.conditions: Giving or receiving a reward for the supply of controlled material is an offence under section 32, which also bars advertising. A transplant from a living donor is an offence under section 33 unless the Human Tissue Authority is satisfied that no reward has been given and the conditions in regulations are met. The gate is the Authority's approval, not residence.
rows.instrument: Human Tissue Act 2004, sections 32 and 33
rows.note: Section 33 carries up to 51 weeks and a fine at level 5.

rows.subject: transplant-prohibition
rows.subject_name: Buying an organ, and being transplanted abroad
rows.conditions: Unlawful to knowingly acquire, receive or otherwise transfer any human organ for valuable consideration. Removal, transport, processing and storage costs are carved out, as are the donor's travel, housing and lost wages. The statute sets no citizenship condition; allocation policy is a separate matter this project did not read.
rows.instrument: National Organ Transplant Act, 42 U.S.C. § 274e
rows.note: Up to USD 50,000 and five years.

rows.subject: transplant-prohibition
rows.subject_name: Buying an organ, and being transplanted abroad
rows.conditions: Living donation of a kidney, part of a liver or another non-regenerating organ is confined to first- and second-degree relatives, spouses, registered partners, fiancés, and persons evidently close to the donor in a special personal attachment. Trade in organs or tissues is prohibited by § 17, with reasonable procurement and transport costs excepted. The bar on an unrelated foreign recipient is a relationship rule, not a nationality one.
rows.instrument: Transplantationsgesetz § 8(1) sentence 2, with § 17

rows.subject: transplant-prohibition
rows.subject_name: Buying an organ, and being transplanted abroad
rows.conditions: Article 4.2 requires voluntariness, altruism, confidentiality, absence of profit motive and gratuity. Article 8 requires a living donor of full age and capacity to consent expressly before a judge, with at least 24 hours between the signed document and the extraction. Neither article distinguishes recipients by nationality or residence.
rows.instrument: Real Decreto 1723/2012, artículos 4 y 8, under Ley 30/1979

rows.subject: transplant-prohibition
rows.subject_name: Buying an organ, and being transplanted abroad
rows.conditions: Trading in organs and blood is prohibited.
rows.instrument: Human Organ Transplant Act 1987, Part 4
rows.note: Part 4 was read for the trading prohibition; the Act's provisions on who may receive a transplant were not read on this pass.

rows.subject: transplant-prohibition
rows.subject_name: Buying an organ, and being transplanted abroad
rows.conditions: Payment for organs and tissue is prohibited.
rows.instrument: Organ ve Doku Alınması, Saklanması, Aşılanması ve Nakli Hakkında Kanun (Kanun No. 2238), Madde 3
rows.note: Madde 3 was read for the payment prohibition. Türkiye's rules on transplants to foreign recipients were not read on this pass.

rows.note: The Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act 1994 governs, with authorisation committees for donors who are not near relatives and separate provisions for foreign nationals. Indian statute sites returned 403 on this pass and the Act was not read.

rows.note: Iran operates the one regulated, compensated living-kidney donation programme in the world, and it is widely reported to exclude foreign recipients. No Iranian instrument was read on this pass, and this project will not describe the programme from secondary accounts.
